proof: The two equal lateral edges from each ridge endpoint put it on the perpendicular bisector plane of the corresponding square side. The four length-s constraints force the ridge parallel to the opposite base sides: otherwise its length is less than 2s (subtracting distance equations gives the lateral components). Up to rigid symmetry, base corners are (0,0,0),(s,0,0),(s,s,0),(0,s,0), ridge L=(-s/2,s/2,h), R=(3s/2,s/2,h). Thus h^2=s^2-s^2/4-s^2/4=s^2/2; h=6. At height t*h, width in x is s*(1+t), in y is s*(1-t), because faces ALRB and DLRC are planar. Area=s^2*(1-t^2); integrate t=0..1: V=(2/3)*s^2*h=288. The equilateral triangular end faces are NOT parallel; their connector lengths are s,s,2s, so they are not the bases of a prism.
prospective_wrong_prism_formula: Using one equilateral end-face area sqrt(3)*s^2/4 and treating the true ridge2s as a perpendicular prism length gives sqrt(3)*s^3/2=216*sqrt(6), about529.0898.
